cards.front: Recall a key point about Technical Dance Skills
cards.back: Technical skills are the specific physical competences that enable a dancer to perform movement accurately and safely

cards.front: Recall a key point about Technical Dance Skills
cards.back: Posture is the way the body is held and provides the base from which all movement begins

cards.front: Recall a key point about Technical Dance Skills
cards.back: Alignment refers to the correct positioning of body parts in relation to one another, ensuring efficient movement

cards.front: Recall a key point about Technical Dance Skills
cards.back: Control is the ability to manage the body's movement with precision, including speed, direction and dynamics

cards.front: Recall a key point about Technical Dance Skills
cards.back: Balance in a technical sense means maintaining equilibrium during both stillness and motion

cards.front: Recall a key point about Technical Dance Skills
cards.back: Coordination links different body parts and timing to produce clean, accurate movement phrases

cards.front: Recall a key point about Technical Dance Skills
cards.back: Spatial awareness is understanding where the body is in relation to the performance space, other dancers and the audience

cards.front: Recall a key point about Technical Dance Skills
cards.back: Good posture and alignment reduce the risk of injury and improve the aesthetic quality of movement

cards.front: Recall a key point about Technical Dance Skills
cards.back: Control allows a dancer to perform slow, sustained movements and fast, sharp actions with equal clarity

cards.front: Recall a key point about Technical Dance Skills
cards.back: Spatial awareness ensures formations, pathways and spacing are maintained throughout group work

cards.front: Recall a key point about Technical Dance Skills
cards.back: Technical skills are assessed in both the performance and choreography components of AQA 8236

cards.front: Recall a key point about Technical Dance Skills
cards.back: Without solid technical skills, expressive and physical skills cannot be communicated effectively to the audience
